messages.author: 808ead273f2a0fc6
messages.subject: multi-mediation with clustered data
parts:
Hi,

I was wondering if anyone could help with the following... I'm running a multiple mediation model (with some ordered covariates) and all is so far working well (code below).  

However, the data is also clustered (i.e the individuals come from 7 different countries) and i'd like to be able to account for this - I mostly want an idea of the variation in the models between countries.  I see there are a couple of possible options -  multi-group or multi-level models and I've had a few goes but I'm not sure entirely either are possible with the combinations of latent measures, mediation, ordered factors and bootstrapping?

Many thanks for any thoughts!

George

multipleMediation <- 'mat_mh  =~  Mat1+ Mat2 + Mat3 + Mat4 + Mat5
esoc ~ c * mat_mh  + Wealth_index +dependencyRatio+ Pat_Ed + Age_months + sex
esoc ~ b1 * CogS
esoc ~ b2 * SocS
esoc ~ b3 * Dis
CogS ~ a1 * mat_mh    + Wealth_index +dependencyRatio+ Pat_Ed + Age_months + sex
SocS ~ a2 * mat_mh   + Wealth_index +dependencyRatio+ Pat_Ed + Age_months + sex
Dis ~ a3 * mat_mh   + Wealth_index +dependencyRatio+ Pat_Ed + Age_months + sex 
indirect1 := a1 * b1
indirect2 := a2 * b2
indirect3 := a3 * b3
total    := c + (a1 * b1) + (a2 * b2) + (a3 * b3)
CogS ~~ SocS
CogS ~~ Dis
SocS ~~ Dis
'
fit <- sem(model = multipleMediation,  data = data, se=“bootstrap”, ordered =c(“Wealth_index” ,“dependencyRatio”, “Pat_Ed”, "Mat4", "Mat5" ), estimator=“DWLS”)
summary(fit)
parameterEstimates(fit, standardized=T)

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: multi-mediation with clustered data
parts: multi-group or multi-level models and I've had a few goes but I'm not sure entirely either are possible with the combinations of latent measures, mediation, ordered factors and bootstrapping?

Multilevel is not available in lavaan for ordinal outcomes.  Even if it were, level-2 N=7 is a really bad idea.  Better to regress all observed variables on 6 dummy codes to control for their (average) effects. 

But multigroup is an option, if you have a substantial N (e.g., 500+ for stable DWLS results) in each group, and that would give you an idea about between-country variability.  But between-country comparisons will only be possible if (at least partial) measurement invariance of mat_mh holds across countries.  Bootstrapping works fine with multigroup models, too.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
